html:
A German engineering company founded in Berlin in 1847 by Werner von Siemens and the mechanic Johann Georg Halske. It began as a small workshop making telegraphs and became one of the largest industrial firms in the world.

Its first product was an improved pointer telegraph. The firm soon built telegraph lines across Prussia and Russia, and in 1870 finished the Indo European line from London to Calcutta. Werner von Siemens described the dynamo principle in 1867, which made cheap electric power possible. In 1879 the company showed the first electric railway at a Berlin trade fair, and it went on to make lights, trams, generators and much more. His brothers ran branches in Britain and Russia.

Siemens grew with industrialisation and with the German Empire. In the Second World War it used forced labour, including prisoners from concentration camps, for which it later paid compensation. Today it works in factory automation, rail, medical scanners and power grids.
